title: Why semiconductors are tetrahedral
summary: Octet AB compounds by bond ionicity and atom size, and the crystal structure (coordination) their ground state takes.

concepts.label: Octet compound
concepts.description: An AB compound whose two atoms bring eight valence electrons (I-VII, II-VI, III-V, IV-IV).

children.label: Electronegativity difference
children.description: Pauling Δχ from PubChem: a proxy for bond ionicity.

children.label: Mean principal quantum number
children.description: Average period of A and B: atom size and polarisability.

children.label: Ionicity
children.description: Phillips' spectroscopic ionicity f_i from the dielectric constant; f_i < 0.785 means tetrahedral (Phillips 1970).

facts.text: J. C. Phillips, Ionicity of the chemical bond in crystals, Rev. Mod. Phys. 42, 317 (1970).

concepts.label: Structure map
concepts.description: A plot of compounds on two atomic coordinates that separates structure types (Mooser–Pearson 1959; Phillips–Van Vechten).

children.label: Linear discriminant
children.description: Fisher's line between two classes in the plane.

concepts.label: sp³ hybridisation
concepts.description: Four directed covalent bonds: the reason tetrahedral semiconductors exist; lost as the bond turns ionic.
